messages:
Samira (CS): Quick async standup for Peregrine Retail adoption — yesterday: validated webhook error patterns and trace logs; blocker: intermittent 503s on /v1/embed causing retry storms and downstream rate spikes; today: need eng help to confirm rate-limiter behavior and a short hotfix, cc @Eli and @Priya.

Eli (Eng): I looked at the spans, batching spikes when payloads >2k tokens and in-flight requests pile up. Can reproduce locally. Preparing a small PR to tighten the in-flight limit and reduce default batch size. PR wip: https://git.redwood.internal/p/rate-limit-fix

Priya (Solutions): For CS side we can add client-side retry/backoff as a short-term mitigation. I can patch the JS SDK to use linear backoff (100ms -> 500ms -> 1s) and ship a minor release. Also compiling a short perf summary for the renewal call next week.

Marco (Support): From the support queue: 3 customers reported the same 503 today, Peregrine's renewals team is watching closely. Any chance we can route Peregrine to a lower-batched model variant or a dedicated pool while we stabilize?

Eli (Eng): Good idea. I'm going to canary a config that sets max_inflight=6 and batch_size=4 on 5% traffic. Deploy command I'm using:
```
bin/deploy --service inference --env prod --rev rate-limit-fix-canary --canary 5%
```

deploy-bot: Canary started for rate-limit-fix-canary at 2071234575 — 5% traffic. Logs: http://logs.redwood/streams/rlf-canary. Alerts channel hooked.

Samira (CS): Great — if canary holds for 30m can we bump to 20%? I'll notify Peregrine that we're validating a low-impact config change and that we'll update them within the hour. Adding to renewal notes.

Eli (Eng): Ack. I'll watch the traces and error-rate dashboards. If errors drop I'll promote to 20% and open the PR for review. ETA ~45m.

Priya (Solutions): I'll also push the SDK backoff patch to a release branch so CS can recommend the client update in the interim. Will link the npm/py package once published.

Marco (Support): Ping me when 20% is live and when you have the mitigation summary. I'll send the customer-facing note and copy the renewal owner.

Samira (CS): Thanks all :pray: — keeping this thread as the handoff/source-of-truth. I'll update the renewal doc here: https://docs.redwood/customer/peregrine-renewal and add short FAQ for the customer.

Eli (Eng): (reaction :thumbsup:) posting an update here after the 30m canary window.

deploy-bot: Canary at 5% held for 30m with 40% reduction in 503s on the sample cohort. Next action: scheduled bump to 20% at 2071234586 after manual approval.

Samira (CS): Approved — bump when ready.

Eli (Eng): Bumped to 20% at 2071234589. Monitoring.

Marco (Support): Received. Messaging Peregrine now with the planned steps and expected timeline.

Samira (CS): Update: Renewal call prep set for Tue 10am PT. I'll include the post-mitigation metrics and next steps. If anything regresses tag this thread and I'll escalate immediately.

Eli (Eng): Canary looks stable at 20%, errors down ~55% for Peregrine traffic slice. I'll follow up with the final PR and changelog entry.

Priya (Solutions): SDK patch branch pushed: https://git.redwood.internal/p/sdk-backoff/push. I'll cut release once Eli confirms final config.

Samira (CS): Perfect. Closing the loop for now — will re-open if we see new regressions. Thank you team! :sparkles:
